# Hedgin

> Hedgin runs Solana vaults with program-enforced custody. Depositors request deposits and withdrawals; whitelisted managers deploy vault assets through Jupiter swaps, Meteora DLMM liquidity, and Phoenix perpetuals; a keeper values holdings and posts NAV so queued requests can settle. Manager bots automate a subset of manager actions through the versioned manager bot API at `https://hedgin.xyz/api/external/v1`, signing every transaction locally.

Key facts for agents:

- Network: Solana mainnet-beta. Every signed transaction moves real funds. There is no public test deployment of the manager bot API.
- Program: Hedge Vault, program ID `r2ahBQ6gbPCJ9FxBymYcXuwXi8NmenRry7SE7QR7FAt`. The program, not the API, enforces custody, roles, and account checks. Program state is the source of truth for balances, shares, NAV, and requests.
- NAV epoch: 4 hours. Deposit and withdrawal requests settle only after a later NAV epoch.
- Amounts: JSON token amounts are base-unit integer strings (`"1000000"` is 1 USDC). Never convert them to floating-point numbers.
- Auth: every API request sends `Authorization: Bearer hv1_<id>_<secret>`. A Hedgin administrator issues keys; there is no self-service sign-up. A key is bound to one manager public key, an optional vault allowlist, an optional expiry, and exact allowed actions.
- Scopes: `read` (GET reads), `send` (relay and status polling), and each builder action by exact name. A build response can name a `next` builder (`jupiter/swap`, `jupiter/sweep`, `dlmm/add`, `dlmm/extend`, `dlmm/add-range`, or `dlmm/zap-out/swap`). The key needs that builder's scope too, or a multi-step flow stops partway. `vault/initialize` also needs a key with no vault allowlist. Phoenix onboarding submission needs both `send` and `phoenix/onboard`.
- Signing: the API builds unsigned v0 transactions with the key's manager as fee payer. The bot signs locally with the vault's current authority key; the server never holds it. The program has no instruction to change a vault's authority, so that key controls the vault permanently.
- V1 boundary: Jupiter swaps, Meteora DLMM actions (positions and limit orders), Phoenix perps (trader setup, onboarding, collateral, orders, sweep), vault creation, settings, manager fee claims, vault close, and strategy setup and close. Request resolution, depositor actions, and admin actions are not in the bot API. A web feature does not imply a bot endpoint.
- Limits: 120 requests per minute per key, 60 per minute per IP, 16 KB request bodies. Build tickets expire after 90 seconds. Status receipts expire after 24 hours.

Manager bot API V1 endpoints (relative to the base URL):

- `GET /vaults` (`read`): vaults this key can manage.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}` (`read`): vault detail: status, fees, limits, pending totals, unclaimed fee shares, and NAV epoch.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/holdings` (`read`): live holdings, valuation, and last posted NAV.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/strategies` (`read`): open Jupiter, DLMM position, DLMM limit order, and Phoenix strategy views.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/nav?limit=` (`read`): posted NAV history; `limit` is an optional positive integer, capped at 2000.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/requests` (`read`): open deposit and withdrawal requests with their settlement state.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/strategy-history` (`read`): closed strategies with their recorded token flows.
- `GET /vaults/{vault}/phoenix` (`read`): Phoenix trader status, markets, open orders, and withdrawable collateral.
- `GET /jupiter/quote?vault=&inputMint=&outputMint=&amount=&slippageBps=` (`read`): swap quote. A swap does not need the deposit mint on either side, but when neither side is the deposit mint, the vault must already track the input mint.
- `GET /dlmm/pools?vault=&query=&page=` (`read`): Meteora pool search.
- `GET /dlmm/pools/{lbPair}?vault=` (`read`): one pool with its active bin, for choosing a `dlmm/open` range.
- `GET /tokens/{mint}?vault=` (`read`): symbol, decimals, price, and verification for any mint.
- `POST /transactions/{action}` (that action): unsigned transaction step or batch, each with a ticket. Actions: `jupiter/initialize`, `jupiter/swap`, `jupiter/sweep`, `dlmm/initialize`, `dlmm/open`, `dlmm/add`, `dlmm/add-range`, `dlmm/extend`, `dlmm/remove`, `dlmm/flip`, `dlmm/claim-fee`, `dlmm/zap-out`, `dlmm/zap-out/swap`, `dlmm/close`, `dlmm/limit-order/place`, `dlmm/limit-order/cancel`, `strategy/close`, `phoenix/initialize`, `phoenix/onboard`, `phoenix/deposit`, `phoenix/withdraw`, `phoenix/order`, `phoenix/cancel`, `phoenix/sweep`, `vault/initialize`, `vault/update`, `vault/claim-fee`, `vault/close`. `vault/initialize` takes no `vault`; the response names the new vault.
- `POST /transactions/send` (`send`): relay `{ transaction, ticket }`; returns signature, receipt, and `pending` or `unknown`. Rejects `phoenix/onboard` tickets.
- `POST /transactions/phoenix/onboard/submit` (`send` and `phoenix/onboard`): hand a signed `phoenix/onboard` build `{ transaction, ticket }` to Phoenix, which co-signs and sends it; same response as send.
- `GET /transactions/status?receipt=` (`send`): `pending`, `confirmed`, `failed`, or `expired`.

Safe execution rules: keep batch order; a step without `sendConcurrently` is a confirmation barrier; follow `next` only after the previous step confirms; after an `unknown` send, poll the same receipt and never rebuild blindly, because a rebuild can execute the action twice.

## Manager bot API V1

- [Manager bot API](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/introduction): What the Hedgin manager bot API V1 does, who it is for, and how its endpoints fit together.
- [Getting started](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/getting-started): Make a first read, build a swap, and send it with the Hedgin manager bot API.
- [Authentication](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/authentication): API key format, scopes, vault access checks, and what to do when a key or manager keypair leaks.
- [Units and views](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/units-and-views): How the manager bot API encodes amounts, prices, bin ids, and public keys, and what the read responses contain.
- [Send and status](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/send-and-status): Sign builds, send them in the right order, follow batches and next steps, and confirm the outcome.
- [Errors and limits](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/errors-and-limits): Error format, HTTP status codes, error codes, rate limits, and request size limits of the manager bot API.
- [Examples](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference/examples): Copyable calls for reads and builds, and a TypeScript loop that signs, sends, and confirms every step of a build.

Each endpoint above also has its own reference page with request and response schemas under https://docs.hedgin.xyz/api-reference.

## TypeScript SDK

- [SDK overview](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/sdk/overview): Install @hedginvault/sdk, create a client, and run a manager action from build to confirmation in one call.
- [Reads](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/sdk/reads): Every HedgeClient read method with its API route, return type, and an example, plus the unit helpers.
- [Actions](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/sdk/actions): Every action that HedgeClient.execute runs, with its request body, notes, an example, and the API key scope it needs.
- [Execute and safety](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/sdk/safety): How execute builds, inspects, signs, sends, and confirms transactions, what the signing policy refuses, and why an unknown outcome is never retried by rebuilding.
- [API checker](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/sdk/api-checker): Run hedge-check-api to probe a live Hedgin manager API for auth, routing, validation, error hygiene, and drift from the SDK's schemas.

## Guides

- [Hedgin documentation](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/): Hedgin runs Solana investment vaults with program-enforced custody. Learn how to deposit, manage a vault, or build a bot.
- [Start here](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/start-here): Pick the right Hedgin tool for your goal: the website, the manager console, the manager bot API, the SDK, or a direct program integration.
- [How the Hedgin protocol works](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/concepts/protocol): Who holds the money, who can move it, and which rules a Solana program enforces for every Hedgin vault.
- [Vaults, shares, and NAV](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/concepts/vaults-and-nav): How a Hedgin vault prices its shares, when requests settle, how fees are charged, and what the status and pause switches block.
- [How Hedgin transactions work](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/concepts/transactions): Why every Hedgin action passes through four separate stages, and why only on-chain confirmation means it succeeded.
- [Deposit into and withdraw from a vault](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/depositors/deposits-and-withdrawals): Request a deposit or a withdrawal on the Hedgin website, follow it until it settles, and cancel it if you change your mind.
- [Manage a vault](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/managers/overview): Run a Hedgin vault from start to finish in the manager console: get whitelisted, create the vault, set fees, invest, handle requests, claim fees, and close it.
- [Swap vault tokens with Jupiter](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/managers/jupiter-swaps): Swap a vault's tokens through Jupiter in the manager console, set slippage, and sell a token back to the deposit token.
- [Provide liquidity with Meteora DLMM](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/managers/meteora-dlmm): Open, manage, and exit Meteora DLMM liquidity positions and limit orders from a Hedgin vault.
- [Trade perpetuals with Phoenix](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/managers/phoenix-perps): Set up a USDC vault's Phoenix trading account, move collateral, place and cancel orders, and wind the account down.
- [Telegram bot](https://docs.hedgin.xyz/managers/telegram-bot): Manage a Hedgin vault from Telegram: wallets, reads, swaps, Meteora DLMM positions, Phoenix perps, and vault settings, with a confirm screen before every transaction.

## Optional

- [Hedge Vault program IDL](https://hedgin.xyz/idl/hedge_vault.json): Machine-readable Solana instruction and account interface for direct program integrations. It is not a list of HTTP bot routes.
- [Web app](https://hedgin.xyz/vaults): Browse vaults and use wallet-driven flows for actions outside the bot API.
